title.narrative: Strengthening Primary Healthcare and Mobile Health Services with Integrated Malaria, WASH, and Nutrition Interventions in Borno State

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed project aligns with the 2025 Nigeria Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) and the NHF First Standard Allocation strategy, prioritising integrated health interventions to reduce excess mortality and morbidity among crisis-affected populations in northeast Nigeria. This will be achieved through the delivery an integrated, community-centered health response to address the urgent needs of vulnerable populations in Borno State, during the 2025 lean season. Targeting 90,000 populations in Goni-Damgari and Bulabulin Ngarnam Communities in Bolori 2 Wards of Maiduguri, the intervention will strengthen access to lifesaving primary healthcare services, enhance disease surveillance and outbreak response, and reduce the burden of malaria and malnutrition through a combination of facility- and community-based approaches.ltbrgtThe project will support one Primary Healthcare Centre (PHC) and deploy one mobile clinic (MC) to reach undeserved areas. These platforms will provide essential health services including treatment of malnutrition, immunizations, deliveries, antenatal and post natal care, provision of Basic Emergency Obstetric and Newborn Care (BEMONC), mental health and psycho-social Support Services (MHPSS) , and referral services in hard to reach areas.lt/pgtltpgtThe MC will serve as a flexible, rapid-response mechanism to reach populations in remote or insecure areas, ensuring continuity of care and timely response to emerging health threats.ltbrgtTo strengthen epidemic preparedness and response, the project will train and deploy Rapid Response Teams (RRTs) in collaboration with the State Ministry of Health. These teams will enhance early detection, reporting, and containment of disease outbreaks such as malaria, cholera, and measles, in line with Health Sector priorities.ltbrgtMalaria prevention will be a key focus, with the implementation of Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS) and larviciding in high-risk communities. vector control activities will be complemented by community-based Information, Education, and Communication (IEC) and Behaviour Change Communication (BCC) campaigns to promote awareness of malaria prevention, hygiene practices, and early health-seeking behaviours.ltbrgtThe project will also address malnutrition through community-level screening of children under five (CU5) and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), with referrals to Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTPs) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs (TSFPs) as needed. Integrated maternal and child health and nutrition counselling will be provided at PHCs and during MC visits to promote optimal feeding practices and improve nutritional outcomes.ltbrgtCommunity engagement is central to the project’s design and implementation. Local leaders, women’s groups, and youth volunteers will be actively involved in planning, mobilisation, and delivery of services. Community health workers and educators will be trained to deliver health messages, facilitate referrals, and support feedback mechanisms. This participatory approach ensures that interventions are culturally appropriate, inclusive, and responsive to the needs and priorities of affected populations.ltbrgtTo support maternal and newborn health and promote safe hygiene practices, the project will distribute hygiene and maternity kits at supported PHCs. Priority will be given to malnourished PLW and caregivers of malnourished CU5, ensuring that the most nutritionally vulnerable households receive additional support to mitigate health risks. All activities will be implemented with a strong focus on cross-cutting themes, including Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP), Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), gender equality, and disability inclusion.ltbrgtBy integrating facility-based services with mobile outreach and community engagement, the project will contribute to the NHF 2025 strategic objective of reducing excess mortality and morbidity, while strengthening local health systems and community resilience in Borno State.lt/pgt
